title: A Prom for the Tryouts
premise: Marguerite Lockridge, statistician for the Ashford Prep basketball team, has survived four years by being unremarkable — until a group chat of classmates begins posting predictions that come true, each one tagged with his name. The chat belongs to students who, like him, were 'chosen' at birth by the Lockridge Trust, an inheritance that pays out only to those who survive to graduation without ever being noticed. As the predictions escalate from pranks to deaths, Marguerite realizes the championship season is a selection mechanism: the Trust culls its heirs through engineered catastrophes, and the prom — the night every heir must be seen — is the final cut. To break the Trust's algorithm, he must do the unthinkable: step into the spotlight, win a game that was never about basketball, and convince the other heirs that survival means refusing the inheritance together.
about_author: P. M. Crane is the pen name of a former high school scorekeeper who spent three seasons charting games in a gymnasium that felt older than it should have. They write young adult fiction about quiet kids who discover the rules were written against them.

chapters.title: The Box Score Never Lies
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. During a routine game, Marguerite notices the point spreads match a pattern he's tracked for two seasons — the team loses exactly when the numbers say they must. He files it away and keeps his head down. Emotional beat: the comfort of routine masking a low hum of dread.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. A montage of invisibility: perfect attendance, lunch alone, a teacher mispronouncing his name for the fourth year. Then a notification: an unknown group chat adds him. The first message predicts tomorrow's fire drill to the minute. Emotional beat: unease cracking open a carefully sealed life.

chapters.title: Six Names
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The chat has six members, all strangers except one — Delia Voss, the team captain everyone adores. Each message ends with a timestamp and his initials. He tests them: the prediction comes true. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Delia Knows My Name
chapters.summary: POV Delia. She corners Marguerite after practice, casual on the surface, testing underneath. She confirms she got the same invite years ago and learned to ignore it — mostly. Emotional beat: the first crack of connection between two people pretending not to be afraid.

chapters.title: The Lockridge Trust
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Digging through his late mother's papers, he finds a trust document naming him a beneficiary — payable only upon 'unobserved completion' of secondary education. Six names. Six heirs. Emotional beat: grief reopening as betrayal; his whole childhood recontextualized.

chapters.title: Prediction Three
chapters.summary: POV Marcus, third heir, a benchwarmer. The chat predicts he'll fracture his wrist at Thursday's scrimmage. He laughs it off — then it happens exactly as written. Emotional beat: denial shattering; the group stops treating this as a prank.

chapters.title: Rules of Invisibility
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The six meet secretly in the library stacks and compare notes: the Trust rewards obscurity, punishes visibility. Every prediction so far has punished someone for almost being noticed. Emotional beat: grim solidarity forming around a shared survival manual.

chapters.title: The Coach's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Delia. She discovers Coach Renner keeps a second set of stats — ones that mirror the chat's predictions perfectly, dated years back. The rigging isn't new; it's generational. Emotional beat: her identity as star player collapsing into complicity.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Almost Seen
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. At homecoming, the chat predicts a 'correction event.' When Marguerite is nearly pulled onstage during the court announcement, a chandelier cable snaps instead — the prediction redirecting at the last second. Emotional beat: terror that the system watches even their small joys.

chapters.title: What Mother Signed
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. A letter from his mother surfaces, written before her death: she tried to buy his way out of the Trust and failed. 'Survive quietly, or survive loudly,' she wrote. 'But you will survive.' Emotional beat: love as inheritance, more binding than money.

chapters.title: The Fifth Heir Quits
chapters.summary: POV Jonah, fifth heir. Overwhelmed, Jonah announces he'll transfer schools to escape the pattern. Within a week the chat predicts his accident on the relocation route. The group races to stop him leaving. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal — there is no exit, only strategy.

chapters.title: Reading the Algorithm
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Using his statistical instincts, he reverse-engineers the prediction pattern: each event escalates toward a terminal node dated the night of senior prom. The championship game is a variable feeding into it. Emotional beat: the statistician becomes the story's analyst — his invisibility skill turned into a weapon.

chapters.title: Renner's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Delia. Coach Renner privately offers Delia a guaranteed scholarship if she lets the season play out as scripted. He claims the Trust protects the school itself. Emotional beat: temptation — safety offered at the cost of the others' lives.

chapters.title: Split the Chat
chapters.summary: POV Marcus. The group fractures: some want to obey the predictions, some want to fight, Jonah wants to expose everything publicly. A leaked screenshot puts all six under school scrutiny — making them visible, which is the one thing they can't afford. Emotional beat: found family strained by fear.

chapters.title: Semifinal, Scripted
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The semifinal unfolds exactly per the hidden ledger until Marguerite, keeping stats courtside, feeds Delia off-script plays through coded signals. They win a game they were meant to lose. Emotional beat: exhilaration — the first moment the pattern breaks.

chapters.title: Correction Event
chapters.summary: POV Delia. The system retaliates: a fire in the gym annex, narrowly missing the team, clearly aimed at the rule-breakers. Renner warns them the next correction won't miss. Emotional beat: victory's cost arrives immediately; the stakes turn lethal.

chapters.title: The Sixth Name
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. He finally identifies the sixth heir — it's been the chat's anonymous admin all along: a student who died two years ago, whose account the Trust still operates. The predictions are generated from a dead kid's data. Emotional beat: horror and pity entwined; the previous cycle's casualty speaking from beyond.

chapters.title: Prom Is the Trap
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Decoding the dead heir's archived messages, they learn the truth: the Trust requires each heir to be publicly celebrated once — prom court, championship ring, something witnessed — before the payout, and the 'witnessed' ones don't survive. Visibility is the kill condition. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the endgame revealed.

chapters.title: Championship Night
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The final game, rigged for a blowout loss that will keep the team invisible — safe but enslaved. Marguerite takes the floor himself, subbing in during a crisis, calling plays from memory of every rigged box score he's ever charted. Emotional beat: the invisible boy choosing to be seen, knowing what seeing costs.

chapters.title: One Second on the Clock
chapters.summary: POV Delia. Tied game, final possession, the gym lights flickering as the Trust's correction event builds. Delia passes to Marguerite — the least likely hero — and he scores as the buzzer sounds. The prediction terminal node fires and fails. Emotional beat: triumph fused with terror; the system now has no script.

chapters.title: The Payout Clause
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. At prom, the Trust's representative appears — the dead heir's guardian — offering a final bargain: accept the inheritance individually and live comfortably, alone, forever watched. The six refuse together, invoking a clause Marguerite found: unanimous refusal dissolves the Trust. Emotional beat: found family as legal weapon; solidarity over survival.

chapters.title: Visible
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Graduation. The Trust dissolved, the money frozen in probate, the six heirs free and permanently marked — known, named, unhidden. Marguerite publishes his full statistical history of the rigged seasons under his own byline. Emotional beat: peace earned loudly; invisibility traded for belonging.
